Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 76 years
Gender: Male

Hospital Course:
The patient presented with a metachronous cancer in the sigmoid colon during surveillance colonoscopy after a previous right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the colon. He had undergone a second laparotomy with revision of the anastomosis due to an anastomotic leak during the immediate postoperative period. During the first postoperative week, the patient developed an enterocutaneous fistula with primary wound failure.

After subsequent management for the non-surgical healing of the fistula for 10 months, the patient underwent an abdominal wall reconstruction with an inlay polypropylene/polyglactin 910 composite mesh that was fixed using polypropylene sutures. The patient remained asymptomatic for 16 months after the primary surgery, after which he was diagnosed with a sigmoid cancer during surveillance colonoscopy.

At surgery, the patient underwent subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis. Several loops of bowel were tightly adherent to the anterior abdominal wall. After separating the loops from the posterior rectus sheath, an enterotomy was made to extract the heavily deposited mesh from inside the bowel lumen. There were no signs of an abscess, fistula, or sinus formation in the surrounding area.

Post-surgery, the patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged in a stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
- Subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis
- Abdominal wall reconstruction with polypropylene/polyglactin 910 composite mesh

Condition at discharge:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.

Follow-up plan:
The patient is advised to continue with follow-up colonoscopies as part of his surveillance protocol.

text:
## Principal diagnosis: **C18.7 – Malignant neoplasm of sigmoid colon**

### Rationale
- **Reason for admission:** Under ACS 0001 (Principal Diagnosis), the principal diagnosis is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. This patient was admitted for a subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis to treat a **metachronous sigmoid colon cancer** found on surveillance colonoscopy.
- **New primary, not a recurrence:** "Metachronous" means a new primary cancer in a different site (sigmoid) from the original right-sided cancer. So it is coded to the sigmoid site, not as a recurrence of the previous tumour.
- **Mesh finding is secondary:** The polypropylene/polyglactin mesh that had migrated into the bowel lumen was found incidentally during surgery. It did not cause the admission, so it cannot be the principal diagnosis.

### Likely additional codes (to confirm against documentation and your edition's standards)
- **Morphology:** M8140/3 Adenocarcinoma NOS, if histology confirms adenocarcinoma.
- **Mesh migration/erosion into the bowel:** T85.6 Mechanical complication of other specified internal prosthetic devices, implants and grafts. Add an appropriate Y83.x external cause code, a place of occurrence code (Y92.22, health service area), and an activity code. Code this only if it meets ACS 0002 (Additional Diagnoses) criteria. Here it did, because it needed an enterotomy to extract the mesh.
- **Adhesions:** K66.0 Peritoneal adhesions, if they are documented as requiring significant intervention. Under the coding standards, adhesiolysis alone may not justify assigning this code.
- **History codes:** Z85.0 Personal history of malignant neoplasm of digestive organs may be considered for the prior right colon cancer, depending on your local and edition-specific guidance.
